arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Slides are arranged in original order in 10 series. Series names are taken from the titles on the original containers that the slides arrived in. Note that while some slides are in chronological order based on slide numbers, slides might be missing from the sequence. Many slides have numbers, but there are slides without number or identifying information. When known, the slide number ranges are noted in the title.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains primarily professional and some personal slides taken during Wayne Freeman's role as an agricultural advisor for the Rockefeller Foundation in India and Nepal. Some slides from the 1940s predate Freeman's time with the Rockefeller Foundation. The contents of the slides relates to various crops, plant breeding, rice, maize, plant diseases and pests, experimental agriculture, agricuiltural machinery, street scenes, fields, landscapes, and personal and professional travel, and family photos.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Dr. Wayne Henry Freeman was an agriculturalist and plant breeder. He was born in 1915 in Kansas. He graduated with his undergraduate degree in agriculture from Kansas State University in 1938. He received his master's and Ph.D. in agronomy from the University of Illinois.

Freeman started his career as a corn breeder at Mississippi Agricultural Experiment Station at Mississippi State University. From there, he joined the United States Department of Agriculture at the Coastal Plain Experiment Station in Tifton, Georgia. He developed Dixie 18, a yellow hybrid corn.

In 1961, Freeman started working in the Rockefeller Foundation's agricultural program in India, and he began a 30-year career in international agriculture work. Freeman was appointed as a coordinator of the All-India Rice Improvement Program of the Rockefeller Foundation and International Rice Research Institute from 1966-1976. His work developed the seed industry in India. In 1976, he moved to Kathmandu, Nepal, as team leader for Rockefeller's International Agricultural Development Service. He remained in that role until 1982 and was an active consultant for another ten years. He retired to Gatlinburg, Tennessee in 1993.
Freeman co-authored a book about his work in India with Badrinarayan R. Barwale titled Seeds of Change: Growth of the Indian Seed Industry, 1961 and Beyond in 2010.
Freeman married Eleanor Glass Freeman in 1938. They had three children. He died at the age of 100 in Gatlinburg, Tennessee on April 7, 1916.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: This material was transferred to RAC by Charles Freeman, Wayne Freeman's son, in 2023 and ingested by RAC as Accession 2023:059.
